subject: AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment: procurement handoff and invoice flow
messages:

Subject: AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment: procurement handoff and invoice flow

Hi Elena / Supply Ops team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — delighted Acme is moving toward an AWS Marketplace SaaS listing. To keep momentum and avoid surprises at activation, I’m sharing a concise handoff checklist and a working metering/fulfillment mapping (attached). Key asks from our side:

- Confirm the Procurement POC for PO and invoicing (name + email).
- Confirm whether Acme will accept AWS Marketplace-managed billing (Marketplace charges on AWS bill) or prefers direct invoicing from Redwood.
- Any special tax/VAT handling or entity information we should record.

What I attached: a short spreadsheet (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx) mapping entitlement events -> marketplace metering events -> invoicing outcomes, plus a sample MPX activation webhook schema. If you prefer, we can run a 30-min call with Soojin (billing lead) to walk through the flow.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm procurement contact + billing preference by EOD Mon (13 Feb).
2) If direct invoicing, share Acme invoicing template (we can adapt).
3) Redwood provides a final fulfillment webhook sample and DocuSign link for the SOW.

Thanks — I’ll pause other steps until we have procurement alignment to avoid duplicate work.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Marketplace
Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks for the clear checklist. Looping in our supply ops alias for visibility. A few data points and questions from procurement: 

- PO contact: Maria Santos (maria.santos@acmeanalytics.com) — she’ll own the PO and invoice routing.
- Preferred billing: We prefer marketplace-managed billing to keep everything on the AWS invoice. Is there any feature loss with that approach vs direct billing?
- Tax/VAT: Acme is US domestic for this contract; VAT not applicable. We will need Redwood’s W-9 and EIN for our records.

Procurement also requested an example invoice and a short note on how seat provisioning maps to usage lines on the AWS bill — our accounting team needs that to reconcile monthly charges. I attached our PO template; please confirm fields you need.

Thanks — if you can confirm the Marketplace vs direct billing tradeoffs and send W-9, we can move to PO issuance.

Best,
Elena Varga
Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Varga <elena.varga@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment: procurement handoff and invoice flow

Elena — really helpful, thanks. Quick answers and next actions below.

Marketplace-managed billing (recommended)
- Pros: single consolidated charge on Acme’s AWS bill, no separate vendor invoice processing, AWS handles tax/CAC where applicable, simpler for finance teams used to AWS consolidation.
- Cons: charges appear as AWS Marketplace line items; some accounting teams need a short mapping note to reconcile itemized consumption -> Redwood product/plan.

Direct invoicing (what Redwood can do)
- Pros: Redwood issues monthly invoice with our remit details and standard terms; easier if Acme requires vendor terms or separate purchase orders tied to our legal entity.
- Cons: adds accounts-payable step and potential delay vs immediate Marketplace billing.

Requested docs: attaching Redwood W-9 and a 1-page mapping doc we use for customers that choose Marketplace billing (link below). Soojin — can you confirm the exact invoice sample and provide the short mapping note for Elena’s accounting team?

Planned next steps:
- Soojin to share mapping note + example invoice by EOD (Tue).
- Elena to confirm whether Acme will proceed with Marketplace-managed billing or request direct invoicing. If Marketplace, Maria can issue PO referencing AWS Marketplace listing (please include the listing ARN in the PO).
- Once confirmed, I’ll send DocuSign SOW with activation milestone for entitlement provisioning.

Links/attachments: W-9 (attached), mapping doc (https://drive.redwood.com/ACME/fulfillment-mapping-v1)

Thanks,
Ben
[Attachment: Redwood_W9.pdf (pdf)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Varga <elena.varga@acmeanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 16:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment: procurement handoff and invoice flow

Hi Elena — quick note from billing: attached is a one-page mapping that shows how our metering events export as AWS Marketplace line items (includes sample CSV and reconciliation keys). If Acme chooses Marketplace-managed billing, accounting will see: date, usage quantity, SKU, and marketplace charge (USD). We recommend PO include: Acme AWS Account ID and the Redwood listing ARN so AWS can tie the subscription to the listing for activation.

If you need a vendor-style invoice, we can issue monthly invoices to the billing contact (Maria) — we'll need the remit address and contact for AP.

I’ll also add the mapping doc to the shared Drive link Ben provided. If that all looks good, Ben: feel free to send the SOW via DocuSign and I’ll enable the fulfillment webhook for canary activation once PO is recorded.

Quick attachments: Redwood_billing_mapping_onepager.pdf

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
